title: Conditional retention tiers and cryptographically verifiable evidence bundling with residency controls
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and define a flexible retention configuration that supports conditional tiers (time-based, sampled, and event-triggered) for prompts, responses, request logs and metrics. Provide automated evidence/export bundles that are cryptographically hashed and signed to support audits, and ensure residency-aware routing for both live retention enforcement and evidence export endpoints.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'retention policies' that combine: 1) tier definitions (hot/standard/archive) with time-to-live and sample-rate parameters; 2) residency constraints (region, tenant, legal-jurisdiction tags) that enforce storage location and export endpoints; 3) evidence bundling service which creates signed manifests (SHA-256) and optional notary signatures for exported snapshots. Policies are applied per-route and per-model, with a retention-preview simulation in the Console that shows projected storage and compliance outcomes. Implement metadata-based selectors for event-triggered retention (e.g., PII-score, escalation flags) and a retention-as-code YAML schema for CI validation.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create retention policies with tiered TTLs and sampling rates via Console and API
Retention policies include residency constraints and cannot route data outside allowed regions for a tenant
The evidence bundling service produces a manifest file with SHA-256 hashes for included objects and a machine-readable audit-summary.json
Exported evidence bundles can be signed by Redwood's export key and include an exporter-assertion header for legal review
A retention-preview shows estimated monthly storage and token cost delta for a given policy applied to historical traffic
Policies support route-level overrides and inheritence with a clear precedence order documented in Console
All changes to retention policies are logged with the actor, diff, and can be exported for compliance audits
milestones: Spec draft and legal review complete (2025-02-18)
Prototype evidence bundling and residency routing (2025-02-28)
Beta with select tenants and telemetry (2025-03-21)
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) internal dogfood + legal review; 2) opt-in beta for tenants with retention needs; 3) enable-by-default for new tenants after 8 weeks of beta telemetry. Provide migration tooling for existing retention rules and an interactive migration advisor that highlights potential customer-impacting changes.
notes: Trade-offs: signed evidence bundles add CPU and storage overhead; evaluate per-export compression and chunking
Consider integration with KMS for per-tenant signing keys in Phase 2
Need coordination with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure residency enforcement in hybrid deployments
Telemetry should include estimated cost delta and sample coverage to reassure customers during rollout
